stories.title: Install LiveKit Agents SDK
stories.description: Install livekit-agents Python SDK and livekit-plugins-all for STT/LLM/TTS plugins. Verify install with a simple echo test. Check if docker/docker-compose available for LiveKit server deployment. Document install path.

stories.title: Install Kokoro-ONNX TTS
stories.description: Clone and build kokoro-onnx from github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx. Download default voice model (af_heart). Verify TTS produces audio from text input. Benchmark latency on CPU. Create simple test script at ~/voice-agent/test_kokoro.py.

stories.title: Verify Faster-Whisper STT Pipeline
stories.description: Confirm faster-whisper is installed. Run a test: take a short audio file (.wav), transcribe it using faster_whisper.TranscriptionWriter or model.transcribe(). Verify output text matches expected. Benchmark transcription speed. Create test script at ~/voice-agent/test_stt.py.

stories.title: Build Baseline Voice Loop (STT → LLM → TTS)
stories.description: Create ~/voice-agent/baseline_loop.py — a working voice pipeline: (1) record audio from microphone, (2) transcribe with faster-whisper, (3) send to Ollama llama3.3:70b via streaming /api/generate, (4) output text to Piper-TTS (fallback) or Kokoro-ONNX (if installed), (5) play audio. Use queue-based architecture with background threads. Target <2s round-trip for simple queries. Add 'Press Ctrl+C to exit' interrupt handling.

stories.title: Add Voice Interrupt Handling with VAD
stories.description: Add voice activity detection (VAD) to the baseline loop using webrtcvad or silero-vad. The agent should stop current TTS playback when the user starts speaking again (interruption). Test: start TTS playing a long sentence, speak while it's playing — TTS should stop and listen. Tune aggressiveness (0=most aggressive, 3=least). Document VAD settings in config.

stories.title: Integrate LiveKit Agents for WebRTC Transport
stories.description: Create ~/voice-agent/livekit_server/ with docker-compose.yml for self-hosted LiveKit server (livekit/livekit or livekit/local-leaf). Start the LiveKit server locally. Create a LiveKit Agent that wraps the baseline voice loop — agent joins a room as a participant, receives audio, processes it, publishes audio back. Test with a WebRTC client (LiveKit's echo example or a simple HTML page). Document the room URL and token setup.

stories.title: Build LangGraph Agent Orchestration Layer
stories.description: Create ~/voice-agent/langgraph_agent/ with the core agentic layer: (1) Define VoiceAgentState schema with conversation history, current task, tool_results, interrupted flag. (2) Build graph with nodes: transcribe → route (intent detection) → respond (llama3.3 via Ollama streaming) → speak (TTS). (3) Add checkpointing with InMemorySaver for fault tolerance. (4) Add interrupt capability — supervisor can send signal to pause agent mid-turn. (5) Implement time-travel: given a thread_id, replay from any checkpoint. Document the graph structure in README.

stories.title: Connect LangGraph Agent to LiveKit Session
stories.description: Write adapter layer ~/voice-agent/agent_server.py that bridges LiveKit AgentSession events (user spoke, agent finished speaking) to LangGraph graph invocations. Map LiveKit's agent_session.user_input_tts_data to LangGraph input. Map LangGraph output state to LiveKit's tts_options for TTS playback. Ensure streaming works end-to-end: user speaks → LiveKit delivers audio → LangGraph processes → TTS streams back → LiveKit plays. Test the full pipeline.

stories.title: Implement Ollama Tool Calling for Agent
stories.description: Add function calling to the LangGraph agent using Ollama's tool-calling API (POST /api/generate with tools parameter). Define these tools: (1) search_web(query) — calls SearXNG MCP server, (2) read_file(path) — reads file from disk, (3) run_command(cmd) — executes shell command, (4) get_time() — returns current time. Test: ask the agent 'what time is it' and verify it calls get_time tool. Ask 'search for weather' and verify search_web is called. Ensure tool results are incorporated into the response.

stories.title: Build MCP Server for Local Tools (SearXNG, Filesystem, Shell)
stories.description: Create ~/voice-agent/mcp_servers/ with MCP tool servers: (1) searxng_mcp — wraps SearXNG at localhost:8888, exposes search(query) tool, (2) filesystem_mcp — exposes read_file, write_file, list_directory tools for ~/ directory, (3) shell_mcp — exposes run_command(cmd) for running shell commands. Each should follow MCP stdio transport. Register them in a mcp_servers.json config file. Test by connecting Claude Code to them with `claude mcp add`.

stories.title: Add Conversation Memory with Checkpointing
stories.description: Enhance the LangGraph agent with thread-scoped conversation memory: (1) Use PostgresCheckpointer or RedisCheckpointer (or file-based if no DB available) to persist checkpoint data, (2) Agent should remember context from previous calls within the same thread_id, (3) Test: start conversation, ask a question, end conversation, start new conversation with same thread_id — agent should remember previous context. (4) Implement memory window: keep last 20 exchanges, summarize older ones into a compressed context.

stories.title: Add Human-in-the-Loop Interrupt Supervision
stories.description: Implement supervisor interrupt capability: (1) Supervisor can interrupt the agent mid-turn by sending an interrupt signal (2) Agent pauses TTS playback, saves checkpoint, enters wait state (3) Supervisor reviews current state, can modify behavior or approve (4) Agent resumes from checkpoint. Build a simple supervisor UI at ~/voice-agent/supervisor.py — a terminal UI showing current agent state, with buttons/keyboard commands: [A]pprove, [M]odify, [I]nterrupt, [Q]uit. Test: agent is speaking, supervisor presses 'I', agent stops, supervisor sees state.

stories.title: Implement Voice Clone with Kokoro
stories.description: Using Kokoro-ONNX's voice cloning capability: (1) Record a 30-second audio sample of Tyler's voice (read a paragraph aloud, save as reference.wav), (2) Use Kokoro's voice cloning to create a custom voice, (3) Configure the voice agent to use this voice for all TTS output. Test: agent speaks in Tyler's voice. Document the voice cloning process and any limitations.

stories.title: Create systemd Service for 24/7 Operation
stories.description: Create systemd user service files for: (1) livekit-server.service — runs the LiveKit server, (2) voice-agent.service — runs the agent server (agent_server.py), (3) mcp-servers.service — runs all MCP tool servers. Use Type=simple, Restart=always, RestartSec=30s. Install to ~/.config/systemd/user/. Run systemctl --user daemon-reload after creating. Document how to check status: systemctl --user status voice-agent, view logs: journalctl --user -u voice-agent -f.

stories.title: 24-Hour Stability Test
stories.description: Run the voice agent for 24 hours continuously: (1) Start all services, (2) Run a microphone listener that periodically sends test queries ('what time is it', 'search for news', 'tell me a joke'), (3) Monitor for crashes, memory leaks, model OOM errors, (4) Log all interactions to ~/voice-agent/logs/, (5) At the end, produce a stability report: uptime %, average response latency, failure modes, memory usage over time. Fix any issues found. Document the test harness at ~/voice-agent/stress_test.py.

stories.title: Write README and Architecture Docs
stories.description: Write comprehensive documentation: (1) README.md — how to start the voice agent, how to connect, how to troubleshoot, (2) ARCHITECTURE.md — full system architecture diagram, component descriptions, data flow, (3) API.md — MCP tool definitions, LiveKit room/token API, supervisor protocol, (4) DEPLOYMENT.md — systemd service setup, environment variables, required ports, Tailscale integration for remote access. All docs go in ~/voice-agent/docs/.

stories.title: Optimize Latency — Target Sub-500ms
stories.description: Profile and optimize the pipeline: (1) Measure latency at each stage (VAD, STT, LLM first token, TTS first audio), (2) Identify bottlenecks (likely LLM inference at ~8-12 tok/s), (3) Optimizations: (a) pre-warm Ollama model on startup with a silent request, (b) use qwen3.5:9.7b for simple queries (faster) and reserve llama3.3:70b for complex reasoning, (c) stream LLM output to TTS as tokens arrive (don't wait for full response), (d) use VAD aggressiveness=0 for fastest interrupt, (4) Target: p50 < 500ms perceived latency. Document latency measurements before/after.

stories.title: Add A2A Protocol for Multi-Agent Handoff
stories.description: Implement A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol for future expansion: (1) Create Agent Card JSON for the voice agent (capabilities, endpoint), (2) Implement a simple A2A server in the agent using SSE (server-sent events) for streaming responses, (3) Create a supervisor_agent that can receive handoffs from the voice agent for complex tasks, (4) Test: voice agent determines task needs deep research → handoffs to supervisor_agent via A2A → supervisor_agent works on task → returns result to voice agent. Document A2A implementation in ARCHITECTURE.md.
